To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glutamatergically and gabaergetically projecting neurons in the ventral palladium are differentially activated during drug seeking and that these neurons differentially regulate cocaine seeking.

(1) VPGlu neurons are activated during extinction learning, but not during cue-induced reinstatement of cocaine seeking; (2) VPGABA neurons are activated during reinstatement of cocaine-seeking behavior; (3) VPPenk neurons show increased activity during reinstatement of seeking, but not during extinction learning.

the nucleus accumbensectoventral pallidum projection regulates cocaine seeking in mice and that this projection is composed of GABAergic and glutamatergetic neurons that have opposing roles in cocaine seeking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the ventral pallidal complex in the regulation of drug seeking.
how neurons of the ventral striatum and ventral pallidium regulate the seeking of cocaine.
how neural activity in the nucleus accumbense (NAc) is transformed in downstream regions, such as the ventral palladium (VP), and how this information is then used to regulate behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the VPGABA neurons are activated in cocaine-seeking mice and are necessary for cue-induced cocaine seeking in mice.
VPGABA neurons and VPPenk cells promote cocaine seeking while VPGlu neurons are involved in inhibiting cocaine seeking.
the ventral pallidal subpopulations of neurons differentially encode and modulate cocaine-seeking behaviors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VPGABA and glutamateric neurons in the VP have opposing effects on cocaine seeking.
the ventral pallidal glutamatergics are the brake and the GABAergic and enkephalin neurons are the accelerator for cocaine seeking.
the VP is a critical node of relapse, and that different VP subpopulations encode and regulate cocaine relapse in opposite ways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ventral pallidal GABAergic neurons are critical in regulating relapse-like behavior in animal models of cocaine addiction.
there is a cell type specific role of the VP in cocaine seeking.
the VP is a heterogeneous structure with multiple subpopulations that regulate drug-seeking behavior.
